title: Tenant Mosaic Circuit with Tiered Trip Zones and Transparent Proxy Fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a per-tenant "mosaic" circuit controller that supports multiple trip zones (soft/hard/eviction), per-model knobs, and a transparent proxy fallback mechanism. The controller should operate with regional affinity and support multi-region failover while preserving SLOs and minimizing noisy tenant impact. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and a staged rollout template for customer-safe activation.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant circuits evaluate a 5m sliding window and produce three states: NORMAL, SOFT_DEGRADED, HARD_TRIPPED; thresholds configurable per-tenant and per-model
Soft-degrade routes traffic to shadowed rate-limited model variants (quantized or cheaper) while preserving up to 90% of lexical fidelity for top-k outputs
Hard-trip routes to transparent proxy fallback (cached completions or edge-hosted micro-model) with request headers indicating fallback reason
Circuit state persisted to Redis leader shard and replicated to local region caches within 500ms for decision locality
Exposed metrics: tenant.circuit.state, tenant.circuit.trip_reason, tenant.circuit.latency_p95, tenant.circuit.error_rate with tag dimensions {region, model, tier}
Automated chaos tests simulate a model dependency outage and verify graceful failover without SLO violation for high-tier tenants (error_rate <= 1% or latency_p95 <= SLO +10%)
Feature flag gated rollout with canary (1% tenants), ramp to 10% with health gates, and rollback plan documented
engineering_notes: We will implement a two-tier decision path: a local fast-path using an LRU-backed region cache for sub-1ms check, and a central authority (CircuitManager) for writes and cross-region coordination.
State: store trip metadata as a small JSON blob in Redis with keyspaced TTLs. Use versioned keys to simplify migrations. Local cache refresh via pub/sub for near-real-time propagation.

Trip logic: compute both incident_rate and latency_violation_score. An example soft trip when: incident_rate > tenant.soft_trip_err_rate OR latency_p95 > tenant.soft_trip_latency for 5m. Hard trip requires sustained violation for 2 consecutive 1m windows or a spike detector (z-score > 5).

Fallbacks: Soft -> rate-limited cheaper model OR prefix-KV cache hits; Hard -> proxy fallback that serves from deterministic cached responses, and if none, runs micro-model (cpu-quantized) hosted at edge region.

Compatibility: New circuit layer must be inserted before request routing to model pools so that routing decisions use adjusted model candidate lists. Ensure function/tool calling and streaming are preserved during fallback (stream fallback semantics defined).
Telemetry: emit structured tags for auditing and billing (fallback_cost_adjustment boolean, fallback_model_id); ensure token accounting is preserved for accurate billing even during fallback.
Security: fallback proxy must respect tenant RBAC and KMS policies. Customer PII must not be logged; use redaction hooks in fallback path.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary - 3 internal tenants, monitor circuit metrics for 48 hours
Phase 2: Customer canary 1% of production tenants, ramp to 5% after 24h healthy
Phase 3: Roll to 25% with additional lower-tier tenants excluded; monitor cost delta and model-quality regressions via evaluation harness
Phase 4: Global on by tenant tier with automated policy sync and documentation for SRE on-call runbook
Rollback: disable flag, and run forced reconciliation to clear soft degraded tokens within 30s
test_plan: Unit tests for trip-calculator with synthetic latency and error traces
Integration test: local cache pub/sub and Redis persistence test using test harness cluster
Load test: spike simulation to 10x normal traffic for 10 minutes, verify soft/hard transitions and fallback correctness
Chaos test: kill model-serving replicas in eu-west-1 and assert multi-region failover is triggered and no P0 SLO breach for premium tenants
Quality gate: run prompt-based evaluation comparing top-3 golden responses vs fallback outputs; acceptable KL divergence threshold configured per tenant tier
dependencies: PM-442 (pricing and billing adjustments for fallback cost accounting)
SEC-77 (KMS policy check for proxy micro-model execution)
